title: The client lifecycle and the multi-server chatbot
intro: Connect, initialize, list, call — then scale the same ritual to many servers with one config file.

steps.title: The ritual
steps.body:
```python
async with stdio_client(server_params) as (read, write):
    async with ClientSession(read, write) as session:
        await session.initialize()
        tools = await session.list_tools()
        result = await session.call_tool("search_papers", arguments={...})
```

For stdio, `stdio_client` **launches the server as a subprocess** and returns the read/write streams; the `ClientSession` runs the 1:1 connection.

steps.title: The chatbot, slimmed
steps.body: `MCP_ChatBot` keeps just `process_query` and `chat_loop` — tool definitions and execution moved to the server. Each server tool's name/description/schema joins the LLM's tool list; when the model requests one, the client dispatches the call through the right session and feeds the result back into the conversation.

steps.title: Many servers, one config
steps.body: Hardcoded server params don't scale. `server_config.json` declares each server; the chatbot opens **one session per entry** and aggregates all tools:

points.label: research
points.note: command: uv, args: [run, research_server.py] — your own server.

points.label: filesystem
points.note: npx -y @modelcontextprotocol/server-filesystem . — official reference server; '.' scopes it to the current directory.

points.label: fetch
points.note: uvx mcp-server-fetch — fetch a URL, get its contents as markdown. npx/uvx install these on the fly.

steps.title: Free capabilities
steps.body:
The official servers repo carries reference implementations and thousands of community servers — the chatbot gained file access and web fetch **without writing a line of tool code**.

> [!warn] The failure to remember: a server that isn't in the config gets no session — and its tools silently never appear. Debug missing tools at the config first.

recap:
**connect → initialize → list_tools → call_tool, once per configured server.**

- stdio clients launch their servers as subprocesses.
- The chatbot aggregates every server's tools into one LLM tool list, dispatching by session.
- server_config.json makes servers data, not code.
- Reference servers = real capabilities for free.
